content: It includes studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and WHO guidelines. 1. Hwang TJ and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the safety of cycloserine and terizidone in the treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013. 2. Hwang TJ, Dotsenko S, and their team analyzed the safety and availability of clofazimine for treating multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis. This study included a review of published guidelines and a meta-analysis of cohort studies, published in BMJ Open in 2014. 3. Katiyar SK and colleagues performed a randomized controlled trial to assess the efficacy of high-dose isoniazid as an adjunct therapy for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. The results were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2008. 4. Van Toorn R and collaborators investigated the outcomes of short, intensified treatment regimens in children with drug-susceptible tuberculous meningitis. Their findings were published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2014. 5. Niehaus AJ and colleagues reported a high prevalence of mutations in the inhA promoter region among patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. This study was published in PLoS One in 2015. 6. Banerjee A and co-authors identified the inhA gene as a target for isoniazid and ethionamide in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This groundbreaking research was published in Science in 1994. 7. Hugonnet JE and Blanchard JS demonstrated the irreversible inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis beta-lactamase by clavulanate. Their study was published in Biochemistry in 2007. 8. Solapure S and colleagues evaluated the in vitro and in vivo efficacy of beta-lactams against replicating and non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2013. 9. Chambers HF and collaborators assessed the activity of amoxicillin/clavulanate in patients with tuberculosis. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1998. 10. Donald PR and colleagues investigated the early bactericidal activity of amoxicillin combined with clavulanic acid in patients with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. Their findings were published in the Scandinavian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2001. 11. The WHO released updated treatment guidelines for drug-resistant tuberculosis in 2016, providing evidence-based recommendations for clinical management. 12. Gonzalo X and Drobniewski F explored the potential role of beta-lactams in treating multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis, highlighting the synergy between meropenem and amoxicillin/clavulanate. This study was published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2013. 13. Prescott Jr. WA and colleagues examined the incidence of allergic-type reactions associated with carbapenems in patients with and without reported penicillin allergies. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2004. 14. A cooperative study conducted in East Africa investigated the use of isoniazid with thiacetazone in treating pulmonary tuberculosis. The results were published in Tubercle in 1970. 15. Nunn P and colleagues reported on cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions to thiacetazone in HIV-1 seropositive patients treated for tuberculosis. This study was published in The Lancet in 1991. 16. Andini N and Nash KA demonstrated that intrinsic macrolide resistance in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex is inducible. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2006. 17. Winters N, Butler-Laporte G, and Menzies D evaluated the efficacy and safety of WHO Group 5 drugs for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis treatment. Their study was published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2015. 18. Iannini PB reviewed the cardiotoxicity of macrolides, ketolides, and fluoroquinolones that prolong the QTc interval. This expert opinion was published in Expert Opinion on Drug Safety in 2002. 19. Falzon D and colleagues analyzed the impact of resistance to fluoroquinolones and second-line injectable drugs on multidrug-resistant tuberculosis outcomes. Their findings were published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2013. 20. Thwaites GE and collaborators conducted a randomized pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic comparison of fluoroquinolones for tuberculous meningitis. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2011. 21. Donald PR reviewed the chemotherapy of tuberculous meningitis in children and adults, with findings published in Tuberculosis in 2010. 22. Sun F and colleagues reported that linezolid exhibits a rapid and dramatic therapeutic effect in patients with life-threatening tuberculous meningitis. Their study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014. 23. Falzon D and collaborators reviewed global progress in addressing multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2015. 24. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (19th edition) and the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines for Children (5th edition) were accessed in May 2016, providing critical guidance on essential medications. 25. Gillespie SH and colleagues conducted a study on four-month moxifloxacin-based regimens for drug-sensitive tuberculosis, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2014. 26. Jawahar MS and collaborators performed a randomized clinical trial comparing thrice-weekly four-month moxifloxacin or gatifloxacin-containing regimens for new sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis patients. This study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 27. The Global Tuberculosis Report 2014, published by the World Health Organization, provided comprehensive data on the global tuberculosis burden. 28. Vierenfeldt J and colleagues demonstrated that treatment delays significantly affect the clinical severity of tuberculosis in a longitudinal cohort study, published in BMJ Open in 2014. 29. Harris RC and collaborators systematically reviewed the effect of early versus late treatment initiation on outcomes in patients treated for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2016. 30. Harris RC and colleagues also reviewed the impact of surgery on treatment outcomes for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, with findings published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2016. 31. Mitnick CD and collaborators updated the research agenda for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis. This study was published in PLOS One in 2016. 32. Guidelines on the management of latent tuberculosis infection were accessed in May 2016, providing critical recommendations for clinical practice.
